Apple TV has just added a batch of classic movies for its subscribers, a move that comes ahead of a particularly strong fall movie lineup.

Apple TV Adds New Movies Ahead of Big Fall Lineup

Movies are hot right now. Box office hits like Oedipus, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and Obsession suggest a cultural moment where cinema is enjoying a sustained surge in popularity.

Apple appears to be positioning itself to capitalize on this trend.

This week, Apple TV added a large number of classic movies for free to its subscribers. The titles vary slightly by region, but in the US, notable additions include The Martian, Arrival, Gone Girl, The Big Sick, Memories of Murder, and 21 Jump Street, among other acclaimed hits.

With this latest batch of additions, Apple's library nearly doubled in size overnight.

Acquiring the rights to these movies doesn't mean Apple is abandoning its own original films. In fact, this sudden influx of new titles comes just ahead of a fall slate of brand-new movies.

Apple TV's fall lineup will see six new films roll out:

  • September 4: Mayday
  • October 2: The Last First: Winter K2
  • October 9: Matchbox The Movie
  • October 16: Tenzing
  • November 13: Being Heumann
  • November 25: Way of the Warrior Kid

Apple has long balanced its film strategy between Oscar fare and crowd-pleasing popcorn movies. This fall, it is pursuing both, and the split is fairly even.

Mayday, Matchbox, and Way of the Warrior Kid look like lighthearted action-comedies starring the likes of Ryan Reynolds and John Cena, while Being Heumann, Tenzing, and The Last First are clearly eyeing awards season.

Apple continues to enjoy considerable success on the series front, with recent returns like Ted Lasso. How it fares on the film side is well worth watching.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, with discounts available through an Apple One bundle.
